definitions.explanation: A very steep or vertical rock face. Used for natural cliffs and metaphorically for extreme, precarious situations.

examples.japanese: {絶壁|ぜっぺき}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{海|うみ}→海：00556_umi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見下|みお}ろした→見下ろす：04569_miorosu⟧。
examples.english: I looked down at the sea from the cliff.

examples.japanese: ⟦{道|みち}→道：00505_michi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{片側|かたがわ}→片側：20150_katagawa⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{切|き}り{立|た}った{絶壁|ぜっぺき}だった。
examples.english: One side of the road was a sheer cliff.

examples.japanese: ⟦ロック→ロック：08116_rokku⟧クライマーたち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{絶壁|ぜっぺき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{挑|いど}んでいる→挑む：12708_idomu⟧⟦{姿|すがた}→姿：03363_sugata⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{圧巻|あっかん}→圧巻：12012_akkan⟧だった。
examples.english: The sight of the rock climbers tackling the sheer cliff face was spectacular.

notes:
USAGE:
{絶壁|ぜっぺき} emphasizes the extreme steepness or verticality of a cliff. Compare with ⟦{崖|がけ}→崖：05391_gake⟧ (cliff, general) which does not necessarily imply a vertical face.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {切|き}り{立|た}った{絶壁|ぜっぺき} (a sheer, towering cliff)
- ⟦{断崖|だんがい}→断崖：05039_dangai⟧{絶壁|ぜっぺき} (precipitous cliff — a set phrase combining two near-synonyms for emphasis)
- {絶壁|ぜっぺき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧よじ{登|のぼ}る (to scramble up a cliff face)

SLANG:
In casual speech, {絶壁|ぜっぺき} is sometimes used humorously to describe the back of someone's head when it is very flat (⟦{後頭部|こうとうぶ}→後頭部：19509_koutoubu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{絶壁|ぜっぺき}).
